question: Do all lead hours of one operating day share a single issuance/availability stamp that precedes the D-1 14:00 KST basis time, or is the supplied cube stitched from multiple runs?
method: key-only read of forecast_kst_dtm, data_available_kst_dtm and grid_id from the four issued weather members of the frozen archive; no value column, no label, no fit, no metric call

findings.availability_time_of_day: 13:00 KST for every row of every member

conclusions: Exactly one issuance stamp covers all 24 target hours of each operating day, in both sources and both splits. There is no multi-run stitching in the supplied cube.
The stamp is 13:00 KST, one hour before the official D-1 14:00 KST basis time, so every supplied weather value is available at the basis time.
Within-issuance temporal neighbourhood operators over the 24 lead hours of one operating day are therefore chronology-legal.
Spatial operators across the fixed 9 GFS / 16 LDAPS points of one issuance are chronology-legal.

lead_hour is a deterministic function of the target hour under a single daily cycle (lead = hour + 11 for 01:00..23:00 and 35 for 00:00), so it carries no information beyond hour and is redundant with the calendar block.

The V5-PREPROCESS concern that lead_hour is a latency-shifted rather than physical lead is factually correct but harmless here, because there is exactly one cycle per day; it does not create ambiguity or leakage.
Temporal support of individual value columns remains unresolved and is deferred to N29b; it does not gate the temporal or gradient candidates.
